questions.question: Who heads the executive branch of the U.S. federal government?
What is the executive branch's central responsibility?
How long is a presidential term?
What body consists of the heads of executive departments and other designated advisers?
Who becomes president if the president dies in office?
What constitutional title identifies the president's military role?
What is a presidential veto?
choices: A court's reversal of a conviction
Rejection of a bill presented by Congress

questions.question: Why does the executive branch include specialized departments?
choices: Departments replace Congress as the sole lawmaker
Each department operates as an independent country
Different agencies administer different areas of public responsibility

questions.question: What role does the Senate have in many major presidential appointments?
choices: Choosing all appointees without presidential nominations
Approving appointments only after a national referendum
Having no constitutional role in appointments

questions.question: What is an executive order?
choices: A constitutional amendment issued by the president
A Supreme Court decision about agency powers
A presidential directive concerning executive operations within legal authority
A state legislature's instruction to Congress

questions.question: Why is the president's treaty power shared with the Senate?
choices: The Senate negotiates every treaty without the executive
The Constitution requires Senate consent by a two-thirds vote of senators present
The president may ratify treaties only after governors vote
Treaties can never become binding international agreements

questions.question: What limits the president's pardon power under the Constitution?
choices: It applies only to state traffic offenses
It requires unanimous House approval in every case
It allows the president to repeal criminal statutes
It applies to federal offenses and does not cover impeachment

questions.question: Why does an executive agency issue regulations?
choices: To implement laws within authority granted by law
To replace the Constitution with agency rules
To eliminate judicial review of government action
To impose rules unrelated to its legal authority

questions.question: How can Congress influence executive agencies?
choices: By deciding every federal criminal trial

questions.question: What is a purpose of the State of the Union address?
choices: Reporting on national conditions and recommending measures to Congress
Selecting Supreme Court justices by public vote
Replacing the federal budget with a personal decree

questions.question: An agency implements a law Congress passed. Which relationship does this show?
A court finds an executive action unlawful. What does this demonstrate?
choices: Executive action can be subject to judicial review
Executive orders always supersede the Constitution
Courts command the military in every case
Presidential actions are never legally limited

questions.question: A president nominates an ambassador and the Senate confirms the nominee. Which principle is illustrated?
Which comparison of a statute and an executive order is accurate?
choices: Both are enacted by Congress and must be ratified by state legislatures
A statute goes through lawmaking; an executive order directs action under legal authority
An executive order overrides any statute; a statute applies only to state governments
A statute directs only military action; an executive order governs only civil courts

questions.question: Why is the commander-in-chief role not unlimited control over all war policy?
choices: The president can amend the Constitution during any conflict
Federal courts alone recruit and supply the armed forces
Congress has powers over declarations of war and military funding
